summary: Iteration 30: tested the new monitoring, error log and live-order gate features, plus regressions. Backend: new suite tests/test_phase16_t1_ops_gate.py passes 14/14. It covers public health and the DB-down 503 unit test; health/ready permissions with no secrets in the output; cron ops-tick auth, replay and heartbeats; the crons.yml schema; health incidents open, are not duplicated and resolve with duration_s; client-error dedupe, redaction, query-string stripping and the 20-per-5-min cap; spike alert plus cooldown suppression; critical alerts; the admin errors API with filters, ack/resolve audit, reopen on recurrence and 403 for non-super admins; the payment checklist test_mode_not_accepted guard; and the orders gate. For the gate: activate returns 409, stop makes checkout/start and payments checkout return 503 orders_closed, existing orders and refunds still work while stopped, as do catalog and wishlist, finance_admin gets 403, resume without a code returns 422 and with a code succeeds. Sample products are rejected by the cart API. Regression: test_phase15_t1_refund_cancel.py and test_phase15_t1_prelaunch.py pass 13/13 (refund-cancel, last-unit race, lockout with spoofed X-Forwarded-For). Frontend (Playwright, 1920 and 390): the /admin link to ops works; all ops-* test ids are present; Run check, ack/resolve, filters and config save work; times show in ET; no horizontal overflow. Emergency stop from /admin/launch makes /cart and /checkout show the closed notice with disabled buttons. Resume without a code shows an error toast; with a code it reopens checkout. The window error probe created a frontend error_incidents doc. The sample product page shows 'not for sale' with Add to cart disabled.

minor.issue: The spike counter counts every source=server error_event, warnings included. During the regression run, Resend test-sink 429 rate limits (email send_failed warnings) set off 'Server errors: 81/100 in 5 minutes' spike alerts. Spikes should count only error and critical severities, or email warnings should be excluded.

try_send returns True when an email is suppressed outside production, so ops_alert_log records delivered=true for alerts that were never sent. Add an explicit 'suppressed' status so the alert log shows what really happened.
The incident kind is 'send_failed_502' even when the upstream returned 429 rate_limited, which hides the root cause in the error log.

issues: Gate history timestamps use the browser locale and timezone (e.g. '11/9/2026, 2:35:15 AM'), not ET as on /admin/ops
ops-filter-since is a native <input type=date>, not the shadcn Calendar/Popover
service, severity and status filters are native <select> elements, not shadcn Select
Emergency stop asks for the reason with window.prompt; a shadcn Dialog would match the rest of the UI

action_items: Exclude warning severity (or the email service) from the server-error spike count
Record 'suppressed' instead of delivered=true in ops_alert_log when an alert email is not sent outside production
Keep the real upstream status (429) in the email send failure kind
Optional UI polish: show orders-gate history in ET; use shadcn Select, Calendar and Dialog instead of native select, date input and prompt
critical_code_review_comments: orders_gate.accepting(): a pause applies in every environment and the lock only in live environments; checkout.start and payments.start_payment both call assert_accepting. This is correct backend enforcement.
_payment_guard requires is_live_key() and MODE=='live', so test-mode evidence can never verify payment items. Correct.
record_error is fully wrapped in try/except so monitoring never breaks requests. Fingerprinting replaces digits so recurring errors deduplicate. Correct.
health_tick: the alert key for a new incident includes the timestamp; this is fine because incidents open only once per component while one is open. Recovery alerts are keyed per incident.
ops_alerts cooldown relies on the unique index key_1 (m0015) for the insert race fallback. Verified the index exists.
_spike_check runs count_documents on every server error. Acceptable at this scale, but consider caching if error volume grows.
